context_prefix_rationale: TSK_MSRY_* is consumed by SF_MASONRY_EXT_NC_v1 (31 tasks). Using MSRP_ (MaSonry RePaint) eliminates all ID collisions. Verified: TSK_MSRP_* has zero existing usage. Pattern follows established convention: MS = masonry, RP = repaint. MSRP prefix is unique across all context_prefixes_in_use.
scope_summary: Combined condition assessment + prep + prime + finish repaint spec for previously painted exterior masonry wall surfaces (clay brick, CMU block, cast concrete, limestone). Covers condition assessment (visual inspection, chalk rub test, adhesion test, moisture testing, efflorescence scan, tuck-point assessment, mortar joint evaluation), surface prep (power wash 1500-3000 PSI per substrate type, efflorescence neutralization, chalk remediation, failing paint removal, surface repair), state-driven primer (chalk-binding for chalking, alkali-resistant for exposed bare masonry, acrylic stain-block for general RP adhesion), finish coat application (spray_backroll primary — spray-only PROHIBITED on porous masonry, brush_roll fallback), optional elastomeric coating system for CMU/concrete (NOT brick — traps moisture). Uses SF as primary UOM with masonry_type modifier (brick/CMU/concrete/limestone/split_face_cmu). 4 exterior RP substrate states. Condition scale GOOD/FAIR/POOR drives prep intensity. QT2-QT4 (QT5 excluded per masonry NC). Flat/satin sheen. spray_backroll mandatory backroll coupling. Lead-safe RRP gate for pre-1978 buildings. Single mobilization.

relevant_findings.topic: Masonry RP uses same application method as NC: spray_backroll mandatory
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike fiber cement siding where RP changes from spray-only (NC) to spray_backroll (RP), masonry uses spray_backroll in BOTH NC and RP contexts. Spray-only is PROHIBITED on porous masonry (backroll forces coating into pores for continuous DFT per Exterior Application Methods Doctrine Part A section 6). brush_roll is fallback for smaller areas or occupied-adjacent. This means the NC spray_backroll production rates transfer with less modification than fiber cement RP — the fundamental application technique is identical.

relevant_findings.topic: Power washing is allowed and effective on masonry — major departure from fiber cement RP
relevant_findings.finding: Masonry substrates (brick, block, concrete, limestone) are hard cementitious materials that tolerate high-pressure washing. Power wash at 1500-2500 PSI for cleaning existing paint surfaces. Higher pressure (2500-3000 PSI) for failing/peeling paint removal on non-limestone substrates. Limestone requires lower pressure (1500-2000 PSI max) to avoid surface etching. This is a KEY departure from fiber cement siding RP where power washing is PROHIBITED. Power washing on masonry serves dual purpose: cleaning (dirt, mildew, algae, efflorescence deposits) and mechanical paint removal (failing/peeling areas). 24-48 hr dry time required after wash. Moisture testing mandatory before coating.

relevant_findings.topic: Efflorescence is a primary masonry RP concern requiring neutralization
relevant_findings.finding: Efflorescence (white crystalline salt deposits from moisture migration through masonry) is the dominant masonry-specific failure mode in RP context. Active efflorescence indicates ongoing moisture infiltration — MUST resolve moisture source before painting (STOP WORK gate). Residual/dormant efflorescence (staining from past moisture events, no active wetting) can be treated: dry brush loose deposits, wash with dilute muriatic acid solution (NOT on limestone — use phosphoric acid or TSP on limestone), neutralize, rinse thoroughly, dry 48-72 hours. Efflorescence treatment is masonry-specific — does not appear in siding or trim RP specs. Recurring efflorescence after treatment = moisture source not resolved = STOP WORK.

relevant_findings.topic: Four exterior RP substrate states apply to masonry
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior RP uses 4 substrate states from controlled_enums.json: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (existing paint well-adhered, minimal chalk — degloss/scuff may not apply to rough masonry texture, skip prime path possible with verified adhesion), SS_EXT_CHALKING (common on south/west elevations, UV degradation of binder — chalk-binding primer required, full surface), SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (cracking/alligatoring/map cracking — power wash to remove loose, spot or full prime), SS_EXT_PEELING (active coating lifting from substrate — heavy power wash, full scrape, alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare masonry at pH 12-13, full prime). Condition scale mapping: GOOD=SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (1.0x prep), FAIR=SS_EXT_CHALKING or localized SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (1.5x prep), POOR=SS_EXT_PEELING or widespread failure (2.0x prep).
relevant_findings.source: controlled_enums.json substrate_state; SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (4-state RP pattern); SF_MASONRY_EXT_NC_v1/spec.json

relevant_findings.topic: Exposed bare masonry in RP requires alkali-resistant primer — pH 12-13
relevant_findings.finding: When existing paint fails on masonry and power washing/scraping exposes bare cementitious substrate, the surface is at pH 12-13 (same alkalinity as NC bare masonry). Alkali-resistant primer (SW Loxon Masonry Primer or equivalent) is MANDATORY on all exposed bare masonry areas to prevent saponification. In NC, alkali-resistant primer is applied full surface (all masonry is bare). In RP, it is a spot prime path triggered by SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT or SS_EXT_PEELING where bare substrate is exposed. This is a substrate-driven primer requirement — the chemistry of bare masonry demands alkali resistance regardless of NC vs RP context.

relevant_findings.topic: Tuck-point assessment is mandatory — damaged mortar is outside painting scope
relevant_findings.finding: Mortar joint condition must be assessed before masonry RP. Damaged, cracked, or eroded mortar joints compromise the wall's weathertightness and will cause paint failure at joints. Tuck-pointing (mortar repair) is a MASONRY trade operation — outside painting scope. However, ASSESSMENT of mortar condition is a painting scope task because it determines: (1) whether painting can proceed on that elevation, (2) whether mortar repair is needed before painting, (3) whether caulking at masonry-to-trim joints is warranted. Minor hairline mortar cracking (<1/16 inch) is typically paintable. Significant mortar deterioration (missing mortar, deep cracks, loose mortar) = flag for tuck-pointing before painting.

relevant_findings.topic: Moisture testing is critical on masonry RP — porous substrate holds moisture
relevant_findings.finding: Masonry is inherently porous and holds moisture longer than wood or fiber cement siding. Moisture testing is CRITICAL before coating: MC > 12% per ASTM D4263 is a hard stop (no coating until dry). Moisture sources include: recent rain, rising damp (capillary action from grade), internal condensation, plumbing leaks, efflorescence-causing moisture migration, power wash water (24-48 hr dry minimum after wash). Test at multiple locations per elevation — base of wall (rising damp), near joints (water intrusion), areas with efflorescence staining, areas below window sills (splash zones). Masonry moisture testing uses either ASTM D4263 plastic sheet method (qualitative) or pin-type/capacitance moisture meter (quantitative). Both are per-elevation FIXED tasks.

relevant_findings.topic: Elastomeric coating option transfers to RP — CMU/concrete only, NOT brick
relevant_findings.finding: Elastomeric coating system (20-30 mils DFT, 300-500% elongation, crack-bridging) is available for masonry RP on CMU and concrete substrates. NOT on brick — elastomeric's low permeability (5-15 perms) traps moisture in brick, causing accelerated deterioration via freeze-thaw spalling and efflorescence behind the coating. In RP context, elastomeric over existing acrylic paint requires verified adhesion of the existing coating — elastomeric will not bridge delaminated paint. QT3+ only (excluded at QT2). Flat sheen only. Material cost 5-8x higher than acrylic. Requires moisture source assessment (existing efflorescence is a flag). RP-specific concern: if previous coat was elastomeric and is now failing, re-application of elastomeric requires full removal of failed previous coat — do not apply elastomeric over failing elastomeric.

relevant_findings.topic: Masonry texture modifier: smooth vs rough dramatically affects production rates and material consumption
relevant_findings.finding: Masonry surfaces range from smooth (painted concrete block, poured concrete) to extremely rough (split-face CMU, natural stone, rough brick). Texture directly impacts: production rates (rough surfaces require more time per SF — slower roller passes, more spray coverage, more backroll effort), material consumption (rough surfaces have 30-50% more surface area per apparent SF and absorb more paint into texture valleys). Texture modifier: smooth=1.00x, medium=1.20x (standard brick, ground-face CMU), rough=1.50x (split-face CMU, rough stone, textured brick). This is analogous to fiber cement surface_texture modifier but with wider range (masonry rough is 1.50x vs FC roughsawn at 1.30x).

relevant_findings.topic: Block filler is NC-only — RP masonry already has filled block texture
relevant_findings.finding: NC masonry spec includes MOD_MSRY_BLOCK_FILL for CMU substrate (PCA P12 Level 2 Standard Fill). In RP context, block filler was applied during original NC painting — the filled texture is already present. Block filler is NOT an RP task. Exception: if original CMU was never properly block-filled (visible open voids in block), the RP estimator should flag for remedial block filling — but this is an edge case, not a standard RP task. Standard RP assumes adequate fill from original NC application.

relevant_findings.topic: Condition assessment for masonry RP is more complex than siding RP
relevant_findings.finding: Masonry RP assessment includes unique inspections beyond standard siding/trim RP: (1) visual condition inspection per elevation, (2) chalk test (less common on masonry than FC, but occurs on smooth-painted block), (3) adhesion test (ASTM D3359 where applicable on smooth areas), (4) efflorescence scan (masonry-specific — white salt deposits indicating moisture), (5) moisture testing (ASTM D4263 — masonry holds moisture longer than other substrates), (6) mortar joint assessment (tuck-pointing evaluation — outside painting scope but mandatory to assess), (7) crack mapping (structural vs cosmetic — structural cracks outside painting scope). Total assessment: ~25-35 min per elevation depending on size and condition complexity.

relevant_findings.topic: RRP lead-safe requirements for pre-1978 masonry structures
relevant_findings.finding: Masonry structures built before 1978 commonly have lead-based paint, especially on older brick buildings, institutional buildings, and commercial masonry. Unlike fiber cement (introduced ~1987, rarely has lead paint), masonry buildings from pre-1978 era are HIGH PROBABILITY for lead paint. RRP containment is more likely to be activated on masonry RP than on FC siding RP. Power washing masonry with lead paint requires full RRP containment — water runoff contains lead paint chips and dust. RRP modifier: 2.0x on prep tasks involving paint disturbance. EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745 applies. Wet methods required for scraping/removal.
relevant_findings.source: EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745; SF_TRIM_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json RC-001 (RRP = 2.0x)

relevant_findings.topic: No acid cleaning on limestone — phosphoric acid or TSP only
relevant_findings.finding: Muriatic acid (hydrochloric acid) is standard for efflorescence treatment on brick, CMU, and concrete. However, muriatic acid DISSOLVES limestone — absolutely prohibited on limestone masonry. Limestone efflorescence treatment uses phosphoric acid or TSP solution. This constraint transfers directly from NC masonry spec COMPAT-MSRY-006. Limestone also requires lower power wash pressure (1500-2000 PSI max) to avoid etching the softer stone surface.

relevant_findings.topic: Condition scale GOOD/FAIR/POOR maps to substrate states and drives prep intensity
relevant_findings.finding: GOOD = SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (minimal prep, power wash only, no prime needed with verified adhesion, 1.0x prep modifier). FAIR = SS_EXT_CHALKING or localized SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (moderate prep, chalk remediation or targeted scraping/feathering, state-driven prime, 1.5x prep modifier). POOR = SS_EXT_PEELING or widespread SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (heavy prep, extensive power wash paint removal + hand scraping, full prime with alkali-resistant on exposed bare masonry, 2.0x prep modifier). Modifiers apply to prep tasks ONLY — coating application rates are identical once surface is properly prepared.

relevant_findings.topic: Caulking scope is limited on masonry RP — masonry-to-trim joints only
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike fiber cement siding RP where caulking is MAJOR scope (200-500 LF of butt joints, trim junctions, transitions), masonry RP caulking is limited to masonry-to-trim junctions only. Masonry walls do not have butt joints — they are monolithic assemblies with mortar joints. Mortar joint repair (tuck-pointing) is masonry trade work, not caulking. Caulk scope: window/door casing-to-masonry junctions, frieze-to-masonry junctions, utility penetration seals. Polyurethane caulk (Class 25/50) for masonry-to-dissimilar-material joints. LF-based measurement. Significantly less caulking scope than siding RP.

relevant_findings.topic: Surface repair in RP context: crack fill and spall patching
relevant_findings.finding: RP masonry surfaces may need repair beyond what NC encountered: (1) crack filling — hairline cracks filled with elastomeric caulk or masonry crack filler (cosmetic, QT3+), (2) spall patching — small areas where masonry face has chipped/spalled, patched with cementitious patch compound, (3) previous repair blending — feathering edges of previous patch repairs that have telegraph through the paint. Structural cracks (>1/4 inch, displacement visible) are outside painting scope — refer to structural engineer. Surface repair is a prep-phase task at QT3+ (QT2 skips minor cosmetic repair).

nc_task_classification.description: Classification of NC masonry tasks for RP applicability. NC spec has 31 tasks across 9 modules.

DIRECT_TRANSFER.description: Tasks that transfer to RP with prefix change only (TSK_MSRY_ to TSK_MSRP_). Rate and method unchanged.

MODIFIED_TRANSFER.description: NC tasks that transfer to RP with modified scope, rate, or conditions.
tasks: TSK_MSRY_EQUIPMENT_SETUP_SPRAY → TSK_MSRP_EQUIPMENT_SETUP_SPRAY_BACKROLL (rate adjusted for RP context)
TSK_MSRY_POWER_WASH → TSK_MSRP_POWER_WASH (RP scope: paint removal + cleaning, higher pressure range)
TSK_MSRY_CAULK_MASONRY_TRIM → TSK_MSRP_CAULK_ASSESS_REPLACE (RP: assess first, then replace failed)
TSK_MSRY_SURFACE_REPAIR → TSK_MSRP_SURFACE_REPAIR (RP: includes spall patching, crack fill)

NOT_APPLICABLE.description: NC tasks that do not apply in RP context.
tasks: TSK_MSRY_CURE_VERIFY — NC only: 28-day cure check. RP masonry is already cured.
TSK_MSRY_MOISTURE_TEST — replaced by RP-specific moisture test (different protocol for existing paint vs bare masonry)
TSK_MSRY_EFFLORESCENCE_TREAT — replaced by RP-specific efflorescence treatment (different approach for painted masonry)
TSK_MSRY_FORM_RELEASE_REMOVE — NC only: new concrete only. RP masonry has no form-release agent.
TSK_MSRY_BLOCK_FILL_SPRAY_BACKROLL — NC only: CMU block filler. Already applied in NC.
TSK_MSRY_BLOCK_FILL_ROLL — NC only: CMU block filler roll variant.

RP_NEW.description: New tasks created for RP context that have no NC equivalent.
tasks: TSK_MSRP_ASSESS_CONDITION — Visual condition inspection per elevation
TSK_MSRP_ASSESS_MOISTURE — Moisture test (ASTM D4263) per elevation
TSK_MSRP_SCRAPE_FEATHER — Scrape failing/peeling paint + feather edges
TSK_MSRP_DUST_CLEANUP — Post-prep dust and debris cleanup
TSK_MSRP_GROUND_COVER — Ground protection below work zone (scraping debris containment)
TSK_MSRP_PRIME_ALKALI_SPOT — Alkali-resistant spot prime on exposed bare masonry
TSK_MSRP_SITE_DEBRIS_CLEANUP — Site debris cleanup including scraping debris collection

SHARED_RRP.description: Shared RRP module tasks — not owned by this spec.

nc_task_classification.total_breakdown: 10 DIRECT + 8 MODIFIED + 19 RP_NEW + 5 SHARED_RRP + 6 from NC cleanup/final = 48

configuration_dimensions.notes: QT5 excluded — masonry wall field is utilitarian surface. QT2=economy single finish coat (acrylic only). QT3=standard 2 finish coats. QT4=premium 2 coats with interstage sand + premium materials.
4 exterior RP states. Drives primer selection and prep intensity. Worst-state-wins per v1. Per-elevation if conditions differ.
GOOD=SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (1.0x). FAIR=SS_EXT_CHALKING or SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (1.5x). POOR=SS_EXT_PEELING (2.0x). Prep tasks only.
Drives texture modifier, cleaning restrictions (no acid on limestone), production rate. split_face_cmu added for RP (rough texture variant of CMU).
Acrylic is standard. Elastomeric for CMU/concrete crack-bridging (QT3+ only, flat-only). NOT on brick (moisture trap risk). NOT on limestone.
spray_backroll is primary — spray-only PROHIBITED on porous masonry. brush_roll fallback for small areas or occupied-adjacent.
Flat or satin for masonry. Elastomeric is flat-only.

research_corrections.original_claim: RRP modifier is 1.40x on prep tasks
research_corrections.corrected_to: RRP modifier is 2.00x on prep tasks involving paint disturbance. Calibrated to 2.00x based on actual wet-scraping, HEPA vacuum, and containment maintenance overhead per EPA RRP procedural requirements.

research_corrections.original_claim: Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, surface temp) should be estimation modifiers
research_corrections.corrected_to: Environmental conditions are NOT estimatable — unpredictable at bid time. Excluded from spec entirely.

research_corrections.original_claim: NC substrate_type modifier values transfer directly to RP
research_corrections.corrected_to: NC FAC_MSRY_SUBSTRATE_TYPE values need recalibration for RP. NC distinguishes brick_smooth vs brick_rough. RP collapses to masonry_type + texture modifier instead. Reason: RP has additional texture dimension (previous paint coats smooth out some surface roughness on brick/stone but not split-face CMU).
